spans.label: Name
spans.consequence: lets someone address you by name and sound convincing in any message that follows

spans.consequence: links straight to your tax record with HMRC

spans.label: Address
spans.consequence: places you at a specific door someone could visit or send mail to

spans.label: Email
spans.consequence: lets someone contact you directly while pretending to be your employer or bank

spans.label: Phone
spans.consequence: lets someone call or text you while pretending to be your bank or employer

spans.label: Sort code and account number
spans.consequence: lets someone set up a direct debit in your name

spans.label: Date of birth
spans.consequence: combined with your name, lets someone pass a phone banking identity check pretending to be you

spans.label: Signature
spans.consequence: gives someone a real signature to copy onto other documents

findings.finding: Your payslip and your bank statement do not agree on your income.
findings.explanation: This payslip shows gross pay of £2,840.00 from Northbridge Retail Ltd for July 2026, but the salary credited to the linked bank statement for the same month is only £2,400.00. Lenders and letting agents often query or refuse an application when the payslip and the bank statement do not agree, so this is worth resolving before the application goes any further.
findings.draft: Hi, I wanted to flag a difference between my payslip and my bank statement for July 2026. My payslip shows gross pay of £2,840.00, but the amount credited to my account that month was £2,400.00. This may be a mid month pay date or a one off deduction. Let me know if you need anything from me to confirm the correct figure.
